title: Usage counting
summary: How a billing account's usage is measured. The top row is the runtime: it counts stored readings inside the storing transaction and reports cumulative counts once a minute. The second row is Laravel, which adds only the increase to the account's month. Alerts are counted where they activate and devices are a level read when asked. Retention and the organization limit are settings, not counts.

boxes.label: Storing transaction
boxes.detail: PersistResultCounted inserts a message's observation and diagnostic rows and, in the same transaction, adds the number of rows it inserted to the organization's bucket for the current UTC hour. A redelivered message or a reading the content match skips inserts nothing, so it counts nothing.

boxes.label: usage_data_points
boxes.detail: One row per organization and hour in the runtime's schema: count, reported_count and reported_final. Counts only grow. Rows older than 40 days are pruned by the maintenance loop; Laravel keeps its own totals.

boxes.label: Usage reporter
boxes.detail: ReportUsage picks every bucket whose count grew since it was reported, or whose hour has closed since, and writes usage.data_points.v1 events of at most 500 buckets with cumulative counts. A bucket is final once its hour ended more than a minute ago, and only a pass's last event moves final_through. With nothing to report it writes an empty event every 2 minutes. Event ids derive from the content, so a replay is harmless.

boxes.label: Outbox relay and inbox
boxes.detail: The events are rows in the runtime's outbox, written in the reporter's transaction. The relay publishes them to JetStream in the order written, and the devices-control-inbox consumer posts them to Laravel in batches of up to 100. An answer Laravel would retry fails the whole batch, which is sent again; an event it will never accept is dead-lettered.

boxes.label: POST events/batch
boxes.detail: RuntimeController records each event id in device_inbox first and applies an event only when the id was new. A usage.data_points.v1 event goes to DataPointReports; a payload with an unknown schema version or shape answers 422, which the runtime dead-letters.

boxes.label: DataPointReports
boxes.detail: Locks the bucket's row in billing_data_point_buckets and counts only the increase over the highest count seen, so replays, lower counts and reports out of order change nothing. A bucket is fixed, when first seen, to the billing account whose assignment covered its hour. A bucket of an organization no account ever had is kept and not counted.

boxes.label: Usage::add
boxes.sub: Locks the account, kind and month
boxes.detail: Inserts the month's row if needed and locks it, so concurrent counts serialize. Overage is the part of this quantity beyond the allowance at that moment, max(0, min(quantity, count after - allowance)), and is fixed when counted. A report arriving late for an earlier month is measured against the plan in force at its hour.

boxes.label: billing_usage
boxes.detail: billing_usage holds the account's count and overage per kind and month. billing_usage_shares holds each organization's share under the name it had, kept when the organization is deleted or moves. billing_overage records which plan assignment each unit of overage happened under, which is what invoices price.

boxes.label: Usage::forAccount
boxes.detail: Builds a month's usage per kind with the allowance now, what is left, the overage and each organization's share. Platform administrators and owners read the account's; a manager with Device.manage reads the organization's own counts. Data points carry final, reported_at and stale.

boxes.label: billing_usage_watermarks
boxes.detail: Keeps how far the runtime's reports are final and when it last built one; both only move forward. A month's data points are final once final_through reaches the month's end, which is what invoice drafting waits for. An open month reads stale when no report was built for 300 seconds (BILLING_USAGE_REPORT_STALE_SECONDS).

boxes.label: AlertProjector
boxes.detail: Counts one alert against the organization's billing account when an automation alert activates, in the projector's transaction and in the month the platform records it. Replays return before the count. Nothing here stops the alert.

boxes.label: DeviceLimit
boxes.detail: Devices are a level, not a monthly count. A device holds a place while devices.limit_place_at is set, from its activation being accepted until its deactivation is accepted or it is archived. billing_device_peaks keeps each month's highest count: claims and releases raise it, and billing:device-peaks records the current count daily at 00:15 for a month in which nothing changed.

steps.text: The transaction that stores a message's readings also adds the rows it inserted to the organization's bucket for the UTC hour. A duplicate message adds nothing.
Every 60 seconds the reporter reads the buckets whose count grew or whose hour has closed since it last reported them.
It writes events with cumulative counts, at most 500 buckets each, into the runtime's outbox and records what it reported, in one transaction.
A failed pass is logged and nothing is lost: counts are cumulative, so the next tick reports them. A quiet runtime still writes an empty event every 2 minutes.
The relay publishes the events to JetStream and the inbox consumer posts them to Laravel in batches, retrying a batch Laravel could not take.
Laravel records the event id, so the same event is applied once, and hands the usage report to DataPointReports.
For each bucket only the increase over the highest count seen is counted, for the billing account the organization was on at that hour.
Usage::add locks the account's row for the kind and month, adds the quantity and fixes the part beyond the allowance as overage.
The report's final_through moves the watermark forward. Until it passes the month's end the count is provisional, and it reads stale when the runtime has not reported for five minutes.
Alerts take the same path from Laravel's side: one per activation, counted in the alert's own transaction.
Devices are not added up: the count is the devices holding a place now, and an earlier month shows its recorded peak.
The admin app and the portal read a month's totals with each organization's share and draw them as meters.
